page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 virtual CPUs (32 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory throughput. The system achieved top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in software compilation and image processing tasks. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance, reaching 5123.16 GB/sec for cached read-only operations and 192.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, though uncached write performance remains average at 76.62 GB/sec. Database and key-value store performance is highly competitive, with Redis SET operations reaching a top-tier throughput of 120.37 million operations per second. Additionally, the hardware-assisted matrix extensions enable strong performance in LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing on medium-sized models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.16xlarge offers high memory density and advanced instruction sets that reduce the need for dedicated GPU hardware in smaller AI inference workloads. However, the absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise software compilation pipelines.
